h1: Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai — a Hotel in the Middle of Nimman Within Walking Distance of Everything
intro: Picture a hotel where you step out of the lobby and reach the cafes, restaurants and One Nimman in under five minutes — Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai is a 3-star hotel that many people pick precisely because it sits right on Nimmanahaeminda Road · the rooms are noticeably more spacious than the price you pay, starting at around ฿900/night in normal periods · it scored 8.7 from 642 reviews on Trip.com, and it's the kind of place that "voices from real reviews" praise mainly for its location and value.

body.html: If you had to sum up in one line who Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai is for, the answer is — someone who wants to stay in the Nimmanahaeminda area on a budget they don't have to overthink, who isn't expecting a 5-star hotel but just wants a room that's spacious, clean and comfortable to sleep in, then steps outside and finds cafes, restaurants and things to do within a few paces · the hotel sits on Nimmanahaeminda Road in Tambon Su Thep, has been open since 2011 and was partially renovated in 2024 · it's a 3-star hotel with around 118 rooms, and its average review score sits at about 8.7 from 642 reviews on Trip.com, which counts as very good for a hotel in this price bracket · this isn't a hotel that is itself the destination of your trip, but it's a solid base for people who want to spend most of their time outside the room.

Location is what "voices from real reviews" mention most, and it's the number-one reason people choose this place · from the hotel's front door it's only about a 3-minute walk to One Nimman, a community mall in contemporary Lanna architecture packed with coffee shops, restaurants, gift shops and the Nimman Night Market on weekends · another 8-minute walk gets you to MAYA Lifestyle Shopping Center, a large mall with a cinema, supermarket and rooftop bar · the World Insect Museum is less than 300 metres away, and Chiang Mai University and its health park are within walking distance · if you've come to Chiang Mai to wake up early and go cafe-hopping for coffee, sit and work at midday and walk out for good food in the evening — the Nimman area is heaven, and Mayflower Grande sits right at the centre of it.

For getting around, this location has a big edge · it's only about 7 kilometres from Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX), or roughly a 15–17 min drive · the hotel offers an airport transfer (ask about the fee and timing in advance) and you can easily grab a Grab in Nimman throughout the day since it's a main tourist area · from here it's about a 10–15 min drive to the moat, Tha Phae Gate and the Old City · the Night Bazaar on Chang Khlan Road is about 15 min away · another point many people like is the free parking, which is very hard to find for a hotel in the middle of Nimman — anyone driving their own car or renting one to tour around Chiang Mai can rest easy on that front.

The rooms are another aspect that exceeds expectations for this price level · there are several types to choose from, ranging from Superior King and Superior Twin at around 25 sqm, up to Deluxe Twin at around 32–40 sqm and an Executive Room as large as 44–48 sqm · the rooms are decorated in green and soft pastel tones with wood floors, giving a warm feel rather than the cold sterility of a chain hotel · there's a wide work desk, a TV, a fridge, air conditioning, free drinking water and a rain-shower bathroom with hot water · several voices from real reviews praise the rooms as more spacious than expected, with the fridge and air conditioning working well — for anyone staying in Nimman for a long stretch or coming to work, alternating between cafes and the room, a space this size makes for comfortable living.

"I chose this place because it's just a few minutes' walk to One Nimman, the room was more spacious than I expected for the price, and the staff sorted out a tour booking for me — great value for a central Nimman location."

To go into a bit more detail on the rooms, since it's something people often ask about before booking · the 25 sqm Superior, though it's the entry-level room, is still wide enough to fit two suitcases and move around comfortably, with both a King bed and a twin-bed option depending on the number of guests · stepping up to a Deluxe Twin gets you 32–40 sqm of space, which suits a small family or two friends who each want a private corner · the Executive Room, as large as 44–48 sqm, is the best value for anyone planning a long multi-night stay or coming for a workation, since it has clearly separate areas for working and relaxing · every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, free drinking water and a bathroom with a hot-water rain shower · voices from real reviews agree that the beds are comfortable and the rooms are quiet enough once the doors and windows are closed, for rooms that aren't on the main-road side.

Another thing that makes a stay here fun is what surrounds the hotel · the Nimmanahaeminda area is famous for Chiang Mai's legendary cafes, from tiny specialty coffee shops tucked down sois to dessert and brunch spots where people queue up for photos · stroll down any of the Nimman sois (Soi 1 to 17) and you'll find northern Thai restaurants, Japanese eateries, bars and art galleries one after another · at night One Nimman has a market and event plaza, while MAYA has a rooftop where you can head up for views of the city and Doi Suthep · if you love nature, you can drive or take a Grab up to Doi Suthep–Pui or visit Ang Kaew reservoir at Chiang Mai University in no time · having your hotel based right here means you barely need to plan long journeys each day — step out the door and the sightseeing starts immediately · and if you're tired after a full day of walking, coming back for a massage at the hotel spa before bed is a perfect way to close out the day for unhurried travellers.

Compared with other options in the same area, Mayflower Grande positions itself in the budget-to-mid price group · boutique or 4-star chain hotels in Nimman like U Nimman or Art Mai Gallery offer fully realised design and some have a pool, but their prices are several times higher · meanwhile the hostels and guesthouses in the area are cheaper but have smaller rooms and fewer amenities · so Mayflower Grande lands right in the middle — you get genuine hotel-sized rooms, a 24-hour front desk, a spa and parking, at a price close to a decent guesthouse · for anyone weighing up "location + room space" against "luxurious amenities" and choosing the former, this is the most sensible answer in the area.

On the amenities side, it has to be said plainly that Mayflower Grande is a compact City Hotel, not a resort · there's no swimming pool here and no proper gym — if you're planning to soak in a pool every evening, this place can't deliver and you'll need to look at a resort-style hotel instead · but what it does have is an in-house spa and Thai-massage service, which is handy for people who walk around all day and want to relax their muscles before bed · there's a mini-mart in the hotel, bicycle rental, tour-booking and taxi-calling services, a 24-hour reception and a small meeting room · overall the amenities are complete for a stay where you're not stuck inside the hotel.

On the food side, the hotel has an in-house restaurant called Chili Bistro, open roughly 8:00 AM–10:00 PM, serving Thai food and à la carte dishes, as well as a buffet breakfast · opinion on the breakfast is fairly split across the reviews — some are satisfied that it's complete and filling, but a few criticise that some items are served cold, or that the choices aren't as varied as at a bigger hotel · the upside is that in the Nimman area, with hundreds of restaurants and cafes within walking distance, many people choose to go out for breakfast instead, so it isn't a big problem · if you do eat at the hotel, we'd suggest trying lunch or dinner cooked fresh to order for a better taste.

On service, most voices from real reviews lean positive · the staff get praise for being friendly and helpful, especially with booking tours, arranging transport and recommending places in the area · the reception is open 24 hours, making late check-ins or coming and going at odd hours easy · one observation that comes up is that some staff have limited English, so foreign travellers may need to use a translation app for certain things · but for Thai travellers this is barely an issue, and the team's willingness to help is something that brings many guests back for repeat stays.

Now for something that needs to be said clearly, because it's an observation that shows up repeatedly in reviews — the noise · the Nimmanahaeminda area is lively both day and night, with bars and clubs such as Monkey Club in the nearby vicinity · some guests who got rooms on the road-facing side or the side facing the nightlife report hearing music or outside noise on Friday and Saturday nights · anyone who finds it hard to sleep or is sensitive to noise should ask for a higher floor or an inward-facing room when booking or at check-in, and pack earplugs just in case · on top of that, some reviews note that parts of the decor are starting to look dated compared with the newer-looking lobby, and that the water-temperature control in some bathrooms is hard to get just right — small details worth knowing in advance, but not problems that affect most people.

On price and value, this is where Mayflower Grande genuinely does well · standard rooms in normal periods start at around ฿900–1,400/night and rise during high season (November–February) or festivals like Yi Peng, Loy Krathong and Songkran · compared with other hotels in Nimman with a similar location, this price level alongside spacious 25–48 sqm rooms, free parking and a 3-minute walk to One Nimman is hard to match · for travellers who focus on going out to sightsee and eat, using the hotel only to sleep and shower, the value here is very high.

There are a few things worth knowing before you book · one — if you're sensitive to noise, ask for a higher floor or an inward-facing room from the start, and avoid Friday and Saturday nights if you can · two — if you want an especially spacious room, choose the Deluxe Twin or Executive Room at 40–48 sqm, which cost only a little more than a Superior but give you a lot more space · three — check clearly whether the rate you book includes breakfast or not, because some rates don't, and if you'd rather have breakfast outside, the Nimman area has far more choices · four — during Chiang Mai's big festivals rooms fill fast and prices surge, so book ahead and pick a free-cancellation rate to be safe · we'd suggest comparing prices across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before you book, since the promotions on each platform take turns being the cheapest.

In short, Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai is a hotel that works very well for one particular group — people who want to base themselves in the Nimmanahaeminda area on a comfortable budget, get a spacious, clean room, walk to the cafes, restaurants, One Nimman and MAYA in just a few minutes, with free parking and helpful staff · on the flip side, if you're after a swimming pool, a full gym or a quiet resort atmosphere, this isn't the answer, and you should consider a higher-tier hotel · but if your destination is "the Nimman area" rather than "the hotel itself" — Mayflower Grande offers a balance of location, room space and price that's hard to find anywhere else in the neighbourhood.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Mayflower Grande Hotel in Chiang Mai · what's nearby?
faq.a: It sits at 9 Nimmanahaeminda Road, Tambon Su Thep, in the heart of the Nimman area · just a 3-minute walk to One Nimman · about 8 minutes to MAYA Lifestyle Shopping Center · the World Insect Museum and Chiang Mai University are within walking distance · Chiang Mai Airport is about a 15–17 min drive away.

faq.q: How much does Mayflower Grande start at · what room types are there?
faq.a: Standard rooms in normal periods start at around ฿900–1,400/night · they range from Superior King/Twin (25 sqm) and Deluxe Twin (32–40 sqm) up to the Executive Room (44–48 sqm) · prices rise in high season and during festivals, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Mayflower Grande have a swimming pool?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool and no serious gym · it's a compact City Hotel focused on location and rooms · it has a Thai-massage spa, the Chili Bistro restaurant, a mini-mart, bicycle rental and tour booking · if you need a pool, choose a resort-style hotel instead.

faq.q: Who is Mayflower Grande best suited to?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people who want to stay in Nimman on a comfortable budget and plan to go out to sightsee and eat · couples and cafe-loving travellers rate the location especially highly · it suits people driving their own car since there's free parking · it's not a fit for anyone who needs a swimming pool or a quiet resort atmosphere.

faq.q: What's the noise like at Mayflower Grande?
faq.a: Nimman is lively at night, with bars and clubs nearby · some rooms may hear noise on Friday and Saturday nights · we'd suggest asking for a higher floor or an inward-facing room when booking or at check-in, and packing earplugs just in case if you find it hard to sleep.

faq.q: What's breakfast like at Mayflower Grande · is it included in the price?
faq.a: There's a buffet breakfast at the Chili Bistro restaurant · opinion is split, with some satisfied and others criticising the limited choices or that it's served cold · some rates don't include breakfast, so check when booking · since the Nimman area has plenty of cafes and breakfast spots, many people choose to go out for it instead.
